item.title: 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The National Assembly has received approval from 28 State Houses of Assembly for the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police in Nigeria. The approval exceeds the constitutionally required threshold of 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, paving the way for the transmission of the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the reports received from the 28 state legislatures had been verified alongside their respective votes and proceedings. According to the statement, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, for consideration and approval. The state legislatures were initially given 30 days, ending October 15, to communicate their decisions to the National Assembly. However, Ogunlana said his office would continue to receive reports from the state assemblies until the bill is transmitted for presidential assent. He said, “Following the receipt and verification of the reports, the Office confirms that 28 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill. “This represents more than the constitutionally prescribed threshold of not less than two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, equivalent to 24 States, as required under Section 9 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999.” The clerk explained that the National Assembly had undertaken administrative verification of the reports and accompanying votes and proceedings to establish their authenticity and ensure that they accurately reflected the decisions taken by the respective state legislatures. He also clarified that Section 9 of the Constitution does not expressly prescribe a third reading for a Constitution Alteration Bill, unlike the procedure applicable to ordinary bills. item.title: CDS seeks civilian support, intelligence sharing to tackle terrorism
item.description: The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, has called for the support of civilians and host communities in the fight against terrorism. Oluyede made the call while speaking to newsmen on the sidelines of the 2026 Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) annual retreat on Tuesday in Abuja. According to Oluyede, there is a need for jointness and synergy among all key security stakeholders. Oluyede, whose philosophy for security lays heavy emphasis on synergy, said that jointness goes beyond inter-agency cooperation and also includes the civilians and communities. “It is important for us to continue to emphasise jointness because no single service can do the job alone, it requires a collective effort.” He said the armed forces are collectively doing their very best to make Nigeria safer, adding that what they require from Nigerians are support, prayers and intelligence reports. “If you see anything, you should tell us because everything we’re doing relies on intelligence, and for that, we need community support,” he said. He said the support provided by Nigerians would aid push the country forward on all fronts. He assured Nigerians that things would continue to get better. item.title: Five players who died after on-field incidents
item.description: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. The 30-year-old is sadly not a unique case of a player dying either on the pitch or because of an injury sustained during the match. AFP Sport highlights five such fatalities: Marc-Vivien Foe, June 2003 Cameroon midfielder Foe collapsed after a heart attack during a Confederations Cup semi-final against Colombia in Lyon, France. The former Manchester City, West Ham and Lyon player was carried from the pitch as medical staff tried to revive him with mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and oxygen. After trying to restart his heart for 45 minutes without success he was declared dead, aged just 28. His death prompted improvements in both the testing of footballers for heart problems and the treatment they can receive during matches, including training club medical teams in CPR and using defibrillators. Antonio Puerta, August 2007 Spain international Puerta, 22, collapsed while playing for Sevilla in a La Liga match against Getafe and died three days later from multiple organ failure stemming from prolonged cardiac arrest. It was three months after he had helped Sevilla to win the UEFA Cup. Spanish legend Sergio Ramos has a tattoo tribute to Puerta and wore a T-shirt dedicated to him as Spain won the 2010 World Cup. “Antonio has always been with me. The next game, I went out on the field with his shirt and for a long time after that, I wore one that was dedicated to him,” said Ramos. Phil O’Donnell, December 2007 The Motherwell captain died of heart failure towards the end of his side’s 5-3 Scottish Premier League win over Dundee United in December 2007. The 35-year-old midfielder collapsed just as he was about to be substituted and was treated for around five minutes on the field before being taken to a waiting ambulance. O’Donnell played for Scotland, Celtic and Sheffield Wednesday during his career and his death caused widespread grief in Scottish football, causing a number of fixtures to be postponed. “He was a man among boys in every sense, in his attitude, his professionalism and integrity and sincerity,” his manager Mark McGhee said. Cristiano Junior, August 2009 The 25-year-old Brazilian, who was then the highest paid footballer in India, collided with the opposing goalkeeper when he scored a goal for his club Dempo 12 minutes from time in the 2004 Federation Cup final in Bangalore. Junior, who had moved to India to earn enough money to build a house for his mother back home, collapsed and was immediately attended to by his Nigerian strike partner Santi Martins. Martins stayed with him until an ambulance whisked him off to hospital but he was pronounced dead on arrival having suffered cardiac arrest. “The match continued. item.title: Kogi varsity defends fee hike, cites NELFUND for 4,032 students
item.description: The vice-chancellor of Prince Abubakar Audu University (PAAU), Anyigba, Prof. Salisu Usman, says 4,032 students have been approved for loans under the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Usman said this while defending the university’s fee increase at an investigative hearing organised by the Kogi House of Assembly on Tuesday in Lokoja. The hearing followed a petition alleging arbitrary increases in fees by the managements of PAAU and Kogi State Polytechnic. The VC said the recent fee review was not arbitrary but part of a unified fee structure approved by the Kogi Government for its three state-owned universities. Usman said the review followed a government directive issued in 2024 to harmonise fees across state-owned tertiary institutions. He said that PAAU’s charges were comparatively lower than those of similar institutions in neighbouring states. According to him, much of the controversy centred on medical programmes such as Medicine and Surgery (MBBS), Nursing and Medical Laboratory Science, which require huge investments, particularly during clinical training. The VC commended his predecessor, Prof. Marietu Tenuche, for reintroducing the medical programmes, which collapsed in 2012. He also lauded former Gov. Yahaya Bello for supporting stranded medical students and commended Gov. Ahmed Ododo for sustaining medical education in the state. Usman said that 4,032 students had been approved for NELFUND loans totalling N536.7 million to pay school fees, while another 600 applications were pending. He urged students to take advantage of the scheme, which also provided a N20,000 monthly upkeep allowance, with repayment commencing two years after graduation upon securing gainful employment. Earlier, the Commissioner for Education, Mr Wemi Jones, said the government followed due process in reviewing fees, considering economic realities and the interests of parents and students. Jones said the directive was issued to PAAU in 2024 but implemented inconsistently across departments, prompting full implementation to ensure compliance. He dismissed claims that Kogi State Polytechnic increased its fees, saying its rector had instead reduced accommodation charges by N5,000. The Chairman, House Committee on Education, Mr Idris Maikudi, said the Assembly mandated relevant committees to investigate the petition and compare the institutions’ charges with those of neighbouring states. Mr Bode Ogunmola, representing Ogori-Magongo, called for sustained government support for medical education, lamenting that the only general hospital in his constituency had operated for years without a doctor due to personnel shortages. Mr Jibril Abu, representing Ajaokuta Constituency, expressed concern over the absence of the petitioners at the hearing. He commended President Bola Tinubu for introducing NELFUND to expand access to higher education. item.title: Portugal raises citizenship wait to 10 years for Nigerians, Indians, Pakistanis
item.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom Nigerians seeking Portuguese citizenship will now wait 10 years as Portugal doubles its residency requirement. The new regime, under Organic Law No. 1/2026, raised the qualifying period from five years to 10 years for nationals of Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and other non-EU, non-Portuguese-speaking countries. Citizens of European Union countries and Portuguese-speaking nations, including Angola, Mozambique, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, São Tomé and Príncipe and Equatorial Guinea, will qualify after seven years. The government also scrapped a 2024 rule that allowed waiting time for residence permits to count toward citizenship. The law, passed by parliament on April 1 and signed by President António José Seguro on May 3, took effect on May 19, 2026. Its implementing regulations were approved by the Council of Ministers on October 29, 2026. The shift comes amid a huge backlog with the Ministry of Justice data showing that 690,480 citizenship applications were pending as of June 30, 2026, a 38 per cent increase from last year. About 26 per cent of the pending cases are residence-based applications. Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum, AIMA, figures also show over 242,000 residents from India, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh and more than 263,000 from Angola, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau and São Tomé and Príncipe at the end of 2025. Under the new rules, applicants must prove Portuguese language proficiency, knowledge of the country’s culture, history and democratic institutions, financial self-sufficiency and allegiance to democratic principles. Minister of the Presidency, António Leitão Amaro, said the regulations would ensure full implementation of the law while simplifying procedures through digitalisation. According to AIMA, applicants who filed before May 19, 2026 would still be assessed under the old five-year rule. item.title: 2027: Is Atiku still contesting? – Lere raises questions over ADC campaign
item.description: Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the FCT Minister, Lere Olayinka, has questioned the visibility and preparedness of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 presidential election, asking whether its candidate, Atiku Abubakar, is still in the race. Olayinka raised the questions during an interview on AIT’s Democracy Today on Monday, arguing that the opposition party’s campaign activities lacked the visibility needed ahead of the election. “I’m only seeing one person contesting. I’m not seeing other people. On social media, I asked a question like 30 minutes ago: Is Atiku Abubakar still contesting?” he said. Asked whether his concern was linked to the ADC’s failure to formally launch its campaign, Olayinka said the issue went beyond the launch of campaign activities. “It’s not about launching campaign. It’s about the optics. It’s about feasibility,” he said. Olayinka, who described himself as a journalist and politician with experience contesting elections, said his participation in a keenly contested primary had given him insight into the electoral process. “I’m a journalist by profession. I’m also into politics because I have contested election before, and so I went through the process of primary. I won my primary. It was keenly contested. I won with, I think, about nine votes. So I went through election,” he said. He subsequently questioned what Atiku was doing differently from President Bola Tinubu in terms of campaign mobilisation. Olayinka pointed to the activities of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, who he said had been engaging communities across the FCT and Rivers State in recent days. “Let me give you an example. Yes, election is January. Today is November 2. That means you have plus or minus. You have two months left,” he said. According to him, Wike had visited Bonny, Tai, Oyigbo and Eleme local government areas in Rivers State within 10 days, while a rally was held in Port Harcourt to unveil Rainbow Coalition candidates. He also listed Wike’s recent visits to Gwagwalada, Bwari, Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC) and Kuje, adding that the minister was scheduled to visit Kwali and Abaji. “What is happening in the opposition circle? What is happening?” Olayinka asked. The former aspirant, who said he was from Ekiti State and lived in Abuja, also questioned the ADC’s presence in both locations. “Have you seen ADC doing anything in the FCT? The answer is no. Have I seen ADC in my state? The answer is no,” he said. Olayinka contrasted the ADC’s campaign activities with the Rainbow Coalition, which he said was mobilising support for Tinubu across party lines. He cited Osun State, where he said Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party had established a campaign council comprising members of the PDP, Accord Party, APC and other political parties. item.title: Pepsi Agba Baller Promo: A Winner Every Minute with ₦800 Million in Cash Prizes
item.description: The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo by Seven-Up Bottling Company (SBC) has launched with over 720 winners, including 4 millionaires, emerging in the first live draws for the ₦800 million reward pool across selected participating regions. The promotion officially commenced on October 28, 2026 and began its live prize draws on November 2, giving eligible consumers the opportunity to win cash prizes while enjoying their favourite SBC beverages. The promotion is running across Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara, Osun, Ekiti, Kogi, Niger and Ondo states offering consumers an opportunity to win everyday until January 3, 2027. With ₦800 million in total rewards, the Pepsi Agba Baller promo features a winner every minute from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily, four ₦1 million winners every day, and a ₦10 million mega jackpot winner every Sunday. The first set of winners includes Oluwatoyin , Oreofe and Damilola from Lagos, and Adeniyi from Ogun State, who each won ₦1 million on the opening day of the draws. Speaking on the promotion, Yewande Ade-Alao, Marketing Manager at SBC, said, “At Seven-Up Bottling Company, we are always looking for ways to make our consumers’ experiences more rewarding. With the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo, consumers can win cash prizes while enjoying the beverages they love. We are excited to see consumers already winning, and we look forward to rewarding many more participants in the promotion.” The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo adds excitement to the festive season, rewarding consumer loyalty and giving eligible consumers a reason to look out for the distinctive yellow covers on Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda, Teem and other Seven-Up Bottling Company products. To participate, consumers need to purchase eligible products from SBC with the yellow cover to get the unique code printed underneath. Participants can then enter the draw by dialing *7022# or scanning the QR code on the bottles and promotional materials for a chance to win a share of the ₦800 million prize pool. Consumers can check the winners’ list and verify their winnings on the official campaign website, www.pepsiagbaballerpromo.com . To ensure consumer protection, winners are contacted through the designated promotion number, 0700 134 1104, and will receive a confirmation SMS. For additional assistance or enquiries, please contact Seven-Up Bottling Company’s dedicated consumer support lines: 0805 690 0900 and 0806 690 0900. Follow @PepsiNaija and @sbc_nigeria across all social media platforms for live updates and winner announcements. Since 1960, SBC has grown into a household name with a portfolio of iconic brands including Pepsi, 7UP, Mirinda, Mountain Dew, Teem, Supa Komando, Lipton Ice Tea and Aquafina Premium Drinking Water, SBC continues to drive innovation, create value and contribute to Nigeria’s development. item.title: 2027: Tension mounts in Oyo over suspension of two LG Chairmen in 24 hours
item.description: By Adeola Badru Political tension is mounting in the Ogbomoso zone of Oyo State following the suspension of two local government chairmen within 24 hours over alleged financial impropriety, amid questions about the political undertone of the unfolding developments ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Chairman of Oriire Local Government, Olateju Michael Alabi, was suspended by councillors of the council on Monday, while his counterpart in Surulere Local Government, Isaiah Adegbite, who is serving his second term in office, was also suspended by the legislative arm on Tuesday. The two suspensions, carried out by the legislative councils of the respective local government areas, were reportedly based on allegations of financial impropriety. However, details of the allegations against the affected chairmen remained sketchy as of the time of filing this report. The development has triggered political debate across the Ogbomoso zone, with stakeholders and political observers questioning the timing of the decisions and whether the actions were strictly driven by concerns over accountability or influenced by the emerging political alignments ahead of the 2027 elections. A political analyst, Dr. Femi Awolesi, who spoke to Vanguard on the development, questioned the circumstances surrounding the simultaneous suspensions, suggesting that political considerations might have played a role. The analyst queried whether the actions were genuinely intended to promote accountability or constituted a political witch-hunt, particularly given the perception that the two suspended chairmen were not aligned with the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Meanwhile, efforts to obtain official reactions from the two affected chairmen were ongoing as of the time of filing this report. Political stakeholders have, however, called for calm and strict adherence to due process, urging all parties to ensure that the unfolding situation does not degenerate into a wider political crisis in the zone. item.title: 2027: If elected, there may be no politician in my cabinet – Duke
item.description: *Says Nigeria needs best hands, not political compensation Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, presidential candidate, Donald Duke, has given an indication of the kind of government he would run if elected president in 2027. He said in an interview in Abuja yesterday that his cabinet might contain no politician if that was what it took to assemble Nigeria’s best hands. Duke, who was former governor of Cross Rive State, said the depth of the country’s problems demanded a government organised around competence and delivery rather than political accommodation, patronage or calculations about another election. “If I am going to pick a cabinet, you may not find any politician in that cabinet,” he said. He added that the 2027 election should be less about personalities and political structures and more about what each aspirant proposes to do about Nigeria’s economy, insecurity, unemployment, education, healthcare and justice system. Duke said he was prepared to put competence ahead of the political considerations that often influence cabinet formation because an administration preoccupied with rewarding politicians could quickly become consumed by the next election. “I’m going for broke. When you start putting politicians in your cabinet, you are looking at the next election. You are thinking about the people who will support you. For me, I want the people to support me. If you perform, the people will support you,” he said. He drew on his experience governing Cross River state between 1999 and 2007 and argued that performance could itself become a politician’s strongest campaign organisation. He said his first governorship election required strenuous political mobilisation because he was introducing himself to the electorate. But by the time he sought a second term, his record had largely taken over the work of campaigning. “My first election in Cross River was really tough. I was basically introducing myself to the people, and there were politicians running around everywhere. “But by my second election, I hardly needed to go to rallies. You could feel the mood. People would tell me, ‘Don’t worry yourself; you have proved your mettle.’” Duke said that experience shaped his conviction that an incumbent should not require elaborate explanations when seeking another mandate. “When you prove your mettle, much of the politics disappears. People trust you because they have seen what you can do. “When you are contesting for the first time, people hold on to your words because that is what you offered them. But when you are seeking a second term, they should hold on to your work. Your work should speak for you,” he said. He stated further that he was embarrassed by incumbents who, after spending years in office, still had to campaign principally on promises or lengthy explanations of supposed achievements. “At that point, you shouldn’t have to spend your time telling people what you did. item.title: Finland offers all-expenses-paid trip for singles in 2027 – How to apply
item.description: Finland is offering all-expenses-paid trips to 16 international singles for a four-day experience featuring blind dates, sightseeing and culinary activities in February 2027. The initiative, called Finnish Dinner Date, is being organised by Visit Finland, the country’s tourism board, as part of efforts to promote Finnish cuisine and attract international visitors. The selected participants will travel to either Helsinki, the Finnish capital, or Tampere between February 9 and 19, 2027. Eight winners will be assigned to each city, where they will take part in a series of cultural and culinary experiences, including outdoor activities, sauna visits, sightseeing and group dinners with local Finnish singles. The highlight of the programme will be a group dinner where each group of eight international visitors will be joined by two Finnish singles for a special dining experience. The meals will feature tasting menus developed by leading Finnish chefs. In Helsinki, the menu will be prepared by Adele Kinnunen, head chef of Café Savoy, who has also appeared on Finland’s MasterChef Professionals. In the Tampere region, the menu will be developed by Henry Tikkanen, the restaurateur behind Gösta, who has represented Finland at the international Bocuse d’Or culinary competition. Visit Finland will cover the winners’ round-trip flights, accommodation in private rooms, meals and scheduled activities throughout the four-day experience. However, participants will not be allowed to choose their preferred destination, as the tourism board will assign winners to either Helsinki or Tampere. Despite being promoted as a blind-dating experience, the initiative does not involve a formal matchmaking service or guarantee romantic relationships. Instead, it is designed to bring international visitors and local singles together through shared meals and cultural experiences. The campaign was inspired by a Finnish grocery shopping trend known as sinkkukori , meaning single basket, in which shoppers use pink baskets at selected supermarkets to indicate that they are single and open to meeting people. The trend gained attention on social media, prompting Visit Finland to adapt the idea into an international tourism campaign. According to Heli Jimenez, senior director of international marketing at Business Finland, the initiative is an opportunity to introduce visitors to the country’s food culture. “Food brings Finns together, and now we are inviting travellers to join us in a truly one-of-a-kind way,” she said in an October 20 announcement. How to apply for Finland’s free trip Applications are open to single people aged 18 and above from around the world, except Finnish citizens and residents. Interested applicants are required to complete a two-step application process. item.title: Osun APC rift deepens over separate Tinubu campaign council list
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Some members of the Osun State Working Committee of the All Progressives Congress APC have rejected the newly released Presidential Campaign Council PCC list in the state and questioned why a separate structure has emerged, deepening the rift in the party’s Osun chapter. In a statement signed by the State Publicity Secretary, Wole Adunola, the officials said, “We therefore reject the list in its present form.” Those who co-signed the statement were the Welfare Officer, Deaconess Adesola Ayangbile; the Assistant Organising Secretary, Rasheed Adeniji; and the Ex-Officio member, Abiola Ololade. They said: “We express our strong dissatisfaction with the composition of the list, which, in our view, does not adequately reflect established party guidelines, due process and the principle of inclusiveness required in constituting such an important campaign structure.” Reports indicate that the list is the 168-member presidential and parliamentary campaign council unveiled on Monday by the state chairman, Tajudeen Lawal. It is headed by the party’s governorship candidate in the last election, Bola Oyebamiji, as Director General, with Lawal as his deputy. However, the officials said they were particularly concerned about the “omission of several members of the State Working Committee who, according to the applicable guidelines, are expected to be statutory members of the council.” According to them, “the exclusion of these recognised party officials raises serious concerns about consultation, due process, and respect for the party’s established leadership structure.” The signatories said the list “appears inconsistent with the earlier presidential directive reportedly naming Governor Ademola Adeleke as the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council in Osun State.” “Following that directive, the governor promptly inaugurated a broad-based campaign team to drive the presidential campaign across the state. It is, therefore, unclear why a different structure has now emerged without adequate clarification or alignment with the existing arrangement”, they added. Adeleke, who is associated with Accord, was named state coordinator of the Tinubu campaign by the APC national leadership. He had earlier inaugurated a 344-member council in Osogbo on October 22, an event the APC National Secretary, Senator Surajudeen Ajibola Basiru, attended. Reports said Lawal and Oyebamiji were absent. The officials suggested the new list might be understood differently. “If the newly released list is intended to serve as a Parliamentary Campaign Council rather than the Presidential Campaign Council, its composition would be more understandable. “This distinction must be clearly established to avoid confusion, duplication of responsibilities, and unnecessary friction within the party’s campaign structure.” The officials said the State Executive Committee “remains an integral part of the APC’s organisational framework”, adding that a successful campaign

item.title: Adegbuyi, Akekoromowei, Super Falcons nominated for 2026 CAF Women’s Awards
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria has secured nominations in three categories for the 2026 Confederation of African Football (CAF) Women’s Awards, announced on Tuesday, with Christiana Uzoma, Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei and the Super Falcons making the shortlist. Edo Queens goalkeeper Uzoma is among the nominees for the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year. She will compete against Chloe N’Gazi, Michaely Bihina, Cynthia Konlan, Mercy Sikelo, Fatoumata Karantao, Khadija Er-Rmichi, Adji Ndiaye, Kaylin Swart and Hazel Nali. In the Women’s Young Player of the Year category, Robo Queens and Flamingos forward Oluwakemi Adegbuyi earned a nomination, alongside Benfica and Falconets forward Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei, Romaine Gandonou, Maëva Nyanidjo, Grace-Ruth Sery, N’Sira Ouédraogo, Rose Kadzere, Kautar Azraf, Adji Ndiaye and Winfrida Gerald. The Super Falcons have also been nominated for the Women’s National Team of the Year award despite failing to win the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title. Nigeria will compete against WAFCON champions Cameroon, Algeria, Cape Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Morocco and South Africa for the award. However, no Super Falcons player was nominated in the Women’s Player of the Year category. The winners will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony on Monday, December 7, in Lagos. item.title: Police arrest two suspects, discovered high-tech indoor cannabis farm in Lagos
item.description: By Matthew Johnson The Lagos State Police Command has uncovered a suspected high-tech indoor cannabis farm at a residential property in Apapa, Lagos, arresting a 49-year-old Polish national and a 36-year-old Nigerian in connection with the discovery. The suspects, identified as Thomas Razvickas, 49, and James Chisome, 36, were arrested on November 2, 2026, at about 8:15 am following intelligence received by police operatives. The facility, according to the police, was equipped with sophisticated equipment for the cultivation, harvesting and processing of substances suspected to be cannabis. The Command’s spokesperson, SP Abimbola Adebisi, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that both suspects were residents of the property searched by the operatives. She said the suspects were currently in police custody, where they had made confessional statements and were providing useful information to assist ongoing investigations. The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, CP Tijani Fatai, subsequently visited the scene to inspect the facility, assess the extent of the operation and receive briefings on the investigation. Fatai commended the operatives for their vigilance and effective use of intelligence, reiterating the Command’s commitment to combating drug-related offences and dismantling criminal networks across the state. He also urged residents to sustain their cooperation with the police by providing timely and credible information that could assist in identifying and apprehending criminal elements. The police commissioner assured residents that the Command would remain proactive and resolute in its determination to rid Lagos of criminal activities. item.title: Iran unveils huge billboard with threat against Trump’s life
item.description: Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill US President Donald Trump across Tehran on Tuesday, bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital. “We will kill Trump”, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran, which depicted the US president behind bars with his head bowed. Another billboard nearby showed Trump along with US Vice President JD Vance, special envoy Steve Witkoff, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with bloodied faces and ragged suits against the background of worn-out Israeli and US flags. Dozens of people gathered in the square waving red flags and carrying banners reading: “There will be blood” while calling for revenge for slain supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in US-Israeli attacks on February 28, triggering the Middle East war. New designs of billboards and displays mocking and vowing revenge against Trump and boasting of victory over the United States in the war have frequently been set up around Tehran. In recent days, renewed diplomatic efforts have been underway to bring Tehran and Washington to negotiate to prevent a resumption in fighting which has spread across the region and driven prices up globally. Trump, who on Tuesday faces crucial US midterm elections amid voter discontent driven in part by the Iran war, has said that a deal “could happen”. In the busy Tajrish Square in northern Tehran, an open-air exhibition featured paintings of Trump, including one showing him with his face lying bloodied on the ground as a foot presses down on his head. Another depicted a bomb obscuring his face. Nearby, a life-sized replica of a jail cell has remained on display, with an actor impersonating Trump spending the day inside. An adjacent screen showed images of the damage caused by US strikes on Iran. Tehran accuses Trump of deliberately targeting civilian sites during the war, including a school and a wedding ceremony, killing dozens of people including women and children. State-sponsored billboards and murals have been a fixture of Iran’s public spaces since the 1979 Islamic revolution, used to honour allies, celebrate military figures and send political messages to adversaries, particularly the United States and Israel. item.title: Nigerians will choose the best product in the marketplace – Obi Media to Governors
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, has taken a swipe at the state governors, accusing them of pushing to undermine democracy, warning that any election that falls short of being free, fair and transparent will fail. The Peter Obi Media Office, POMR noted that it had become aware of a series of covert attempts by governors to interfere with the democratic process, just as it cautioned that Nigerians would resist any process that did not meet the required standards of free, fair and transparent elections. In a statement signed on Tuesday by the POMR spokesman, Idris Zekeri, he reminded the governors that, despite their alleged fraudulent efforts, they were presenting a poor product and that Nigerians would choose the best option available in the marketplace. item.title: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm island – Report
item.description: The United States launched limited strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, US media reported, as Iranian media reported five explosions in quick succession. The reported strikes came as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump’s grip on power. The strikes, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, hit Qeshm Island, strategically located in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets. Unnamed US officials cited by the Journal, CNN, The New York Times and several other outlets, described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. It also said they had not been publicly announced to avoid the impression Washington intended to resume major combat operations. US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. The US and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months. Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokespeson told AFP, “No”. Israel also held an election last week that saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party come out on top, but still short of a majority. The reported attack came just hours after Trump signaled a deal with Iran “could happen”, as American voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. It did not say what was behind the explosions. – Ball in US court – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said indirect negotiations were taking place with the US. “Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media. On Tuesday, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has been Tehran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said that while Iran was ready for war it had given Washington a “rational response”. “The ball is now in America’s court to prevent war.” Oil prices had plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict. – Reopen the strait – US Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday. China also called for a return to diplomacy, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin. item.title: Gunmen abduct two visually impaired persons in Plateau, demand N50m ransom
item.description: … as seven escape By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have abducted two visually impaired persons along Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State while they were returning to Jos from Benue State, with their abductors demanding N50 million ransom for their release. The victims were among nine persons travelling in a vehicle to attend a training programme in Benue State, while seven others reportedly escaped when the vehicle came under attack on Monday night. Chairman of the Plateau State chapter of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), Shindol Aaron, who confirmed the incident, said the victims were abducted around 8pm in Riyom LGA. He said, “They were selected to attend a training in Benue State and, from what I gathered, they took off from Jos.” “Along the way, they got information that the event had been postponed to another day, and they were asked to return to their station.” “So, it was on their way back to Jos that they encountered some kidnappers who abducted them.” “They were nine in the vehicle. Seven of them escaped, and two were abducted. So, right now, we have a male and a lady in their custody.” According to him, the abductors had established contact with someone in connection with the release of the victims. He said, “This incident happened yesterday, Monday, in the night, around 8pm around Riyom LGA.” “I have not spoken with the kidnappers, but I was told that they were asking for ransom from somebody who spoke with them.” Aaron said the incident had been reported to security agencies, adding that efforts were ongoing to secure the release of the victims. He said, “We have reported the incident to the security agents, and we are trying to see how they could be released.” “The driver of the vehicle also went to the police station to report.” Another member of the association, Ishaya Ayuba Danjatau, who also confirmed the abduction, said the kidnappers had demanded an N50 million ransom. The member said, “The kidnappers have reached out, and they are demanding N50 million before they can free the two persons in their custody. “Where do they want us to get the money from?” Efforts to obtain the reaction of the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, DSP Alabo Alfred, were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: El Nino Watch: The impacts around the world this week
item.description: With torrential rains in India and Nepal, and drought already devastating South America, this year’s exceptionally strong El Nino is being felt across the globe. It threatens rice and coffee harvests to such an extent that the World Bank expects food prices to rise by 18 percent next year. Here is how El Nino is playing out across AFP’s network. – Cyclone lashes India – Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, killing at least three people and triggering nearly 100,000 evacuations. “Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water,” said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name, after being taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada, close to the heart of the storm. Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean. The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has contributed to unprecedented warming. Cyclone Arnab then moved on towards Nepal, bringing heavy snowfall to the high Himalayan regions and intense rain through Saturday. – Bolivia declares state of emergency – In Bolivia, drought is affecting 78,000 families in six of the country’s nine departments and has led to the loss of more than 75,000 cattle, according to a government report this week. On Saturday, the Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency to free up resources for dealing with the impact of El Nino. “This will be a phenomenon that will have very severe impacts in terms of drought and floods, and we need the cooperation of all institutions,” Paz said. In neighbouring countries such as Peru, El Nino has ramped up temperatures and triggered forest fires that have already claimed the lives of at least 12 people. It has also helped spread the tropical disease dengue fever. In Chile meanwhile it is behind the rainiest October ever recorded in Santiago. – El Nino in numbers – According to the World Bank, food prices are expected to rise by 18 percent between 2025 and 2027, a surge explained both by supply difficulties caused by conflicts and by the anticipated effects of El Nino. Since June, the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab estimates that 484,500 excess heat-related deaths have occurred globally due to the weather phenomenon. The organisation projects about 373,000 additional deaths could occur over the next six months. – Vulnerable crops – Coffee, cocoa, rice… in this “Super” El Nino year, what are the most vulnerable crops? The answer depends on the region, but “from a food-security perspective, the crops of greatest concern are staple foods because they provide the bulk of calories consumed by populations in vulnerable countries,” Maximo Torero, chief economist at the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), told AFP.
